genZNote: So similar to RSV clinically that for years nobody realized it was its own separate virus until 2001.

morphology.shape: Pleomorphic, enveloped virion with helical nucleocapsid

habitat.hostAssociation: Infects the respiratory epithelium, causing pathology similar to respiratory syncytial virus
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans, with young children, older adults, and immunocompromised patients most affected by severe disease

identificationClues: Diagnosed by multiplex respiratory viral PCR panel — clinically indistinguishable from RSV without molecular testing
First identified in 2001, relatively recently compared to most other classic respiratory viruses
Causes a nearly identical clinical syndrome to RSV: bronchiolitis, croup-like illness, and pneumonia, particularly in young children
Also a significant cause of severe respiratory illness in the elderly and immunocompromised patients

diseases: Bronchiolitis and pneumonia in young children, closely resembling RSV disease
Upper respiratory tract infection (common cold-like illness) in healthy older children/adults
Severe lower respiratory tract disease in elderly and immunocompromised patients
clinicalImportance.transmission: Respiratory droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces/fomites
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A major cause of acute respiratory illness worldwide, second only to RSV in relative frequency among young children hospitalized for bronchiolitis; typically circulates in late winter to spring, somewhat later in the season than RSV
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Because hMPV and RSV cause clinically indistinguishable disease, a multiplex respiratory PCR panel is required to differentiate them, which matters for surveillance and for RSV-specific therapies/prophylaxis (e.g., palivizumab) that do not apply to hMPV

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — diagnosed by respiratory PCR panel
examFacts.importantDisease: Bronchiolitis/pneumonia in children, clinically indistinguishable from RSV
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A relatively recently discovered (2001) paramyxovirus-family relative that causes an RSV-like clinical syndrome and can only be distinguished from RSV by molecular testing
